info.title: VRRP
info.description: RESTful interface for AOS-CX switch software

accept_mode_disable.description: Set this value to `true`, to disable the accept mode. If accept mode is enabled, routes for vritual IP addresses will be installed and VR will accept the packets destined to virtual IP addresses. If accept mode is disabled, routes for virtual IP addresses will not be installed hence VR will not accept any packet destined to virtual IP addresses.

active_advertise_interval.description: Specifies advertisement interval in milliseconds which is advertised by active router.

admin_enable.description: Set this value to `true`, to activate the VR instance.

auth_key.description: Authentication key to be used with VRRPv2 advertisements. This does not take effect if the VRRP version is VRRPv3. If not set, VRRP authentication is not operational on that VR.

auth_mode.description: Specifies the authentication mode to be used when exchanging VRRP packets. This is only applicable when VRRP version is VRRPv2.  `text`: a clear-text password is included in VRRP advertisements.  `md5` : an Authentication Header(AH) is added to the IPv4 headers of the VRRP advertisement packets.  `none` : VRRP advertisement packets are not authenticated. This does not take effect if the VRRP version is VRRPv3.

bfd_peer_addresses.description: Specifies all potential BFD peers. Active will establish BFD sessions to all peers. Standby will establish BFD session to the active only.

group-id.description:
Reference Resource: [VRRP](#/VRRP)
The port's VRRP groups (or VR instances) for IPv6 address family. A maximum of `32` VRRP groups can be assigned to a port.

ip_address.description: Specifies a virtual IPv4 or IPv6 address for the VR instance. For an owner, the virtual IP must be one of the IP addresses configured on the interface for that VR. For a standby, the virtual IP must match the virtual IP of the owner. The owner and the standbys using a given virtual IP must all belong to the same network or subnet. For IPv6, VR's first address should be link local address. After the primary link local IPv6 address is configured on the VR, user can add the global IPv6 addresses.  This column, also specifies the interface's IP address to designate as the source for VRRP advertisements from the VR. By default primary IP address of real interface is used as source for VRRP advertisements. Source IP configuration parameter is for IPv4 only. IPv6 doesn't have a source IP address configuration parameter. For IPv6, the source IP address is the link-local address of the real interface over which the packet is transmitted.

ip_address_secondary.description: Specifies secondary IPv4 or IPv6 addresses for the VRRP group. You must configure a primary address before you are able to configure secondary addresses.

preempt_disable.description: Set this value to `true`, to disable preempt mode. When mode is enabled, a Standby router coming up with a higher priority than another Standby that is currently operating as Active will take over the Active function. When the mode is disabled, the protocol prevents higher-priority Standby from taking over the Active operation from a lower-priority Standby. This mode does not prevent an Owner router from resuming the Active function after recovering from being unavailable. Also, the VR instance must be disabled (that is, set "admin_enable" to `false`) when setting this field.

priority.description: The priority value of the VR.

active_to_init.description: Number of times VR state changed from active to init.

active_to_standby.description: Number of times VR state changed from active to standby.

advertise_interval_errors.description: Number of packets discarded due to advertisement interval mismatch.

advertise_recv_in_init_state.description: Number of packets discarded due to advertisements recieved in init state.

advertise_recv_with_invalid_len.description: Number of packets discarded due to invalid packet length of advertisements recieved.

advertise_recv_with_invalid_ttl.description: Number of packets discarded due to invalid "ttl" in advertisements recieved.

advertise_recv_with_invalid_type.description: Number of packets discarded due to invalid value in "type" field of advertisements recieved.

init_to_active.description: Number of times VR state changed from init to active.

init_to_standby.description: Number of times VR state changed from init to standby.

ip_address_owner_conflicts.description: Number of packets discarded due to owner IP address conflict.

mismatched_addr_list_pkts.description: Number of VRRP packets received wherein the list of VIPs doesn't match the locally configured VIPs for a VR.

mismatched_auth_type_pkts.description: Number of VRRP packets received with the authentication type not equal to 0 (zero, which is no authentication).

near_failovers.description: Number of occurences of near failovers on the Standby VRRP routers. This makes visible any difficulties the VRRP routers are having receiving the "hello" advertisement from the active router.

other_reasons.description: Number of packets discarded due to other reasons.

standby_to_active.description: Number of times VR state changed from standby to active.

standby_to_init.description: Number of times VR state changed from standby to init.

vrrpv2_advertisement_rx.description: Number of VRRPv2 advertisement packets received.

vrrpv2_advertisement_tx.description: Number of VRRPv2 advertisement packets sent.

vrrpv2_incompatibility.description: Number of VRRPv2 incompatible packets discarded.

vrrpv3_advertisement_rx.description: Number of VRRPv3 advertisement packets received.

vrrpv3_advertisement_tx.description: Number of VRRPv3 advertisement packets sent.

zero_priority_rx.description: Number of VRRP advertisement packets received with the priority field set to 0(zero).

zero_priority_tx.description: Number of VRRP advertisement packets sent with the priority field set to 0(zero).

active_change_reason.description: Specifies the reason of this router to change to active. * `priority`: Virtual router has changed to Active state because it has higher priority than other virtual routers. * `preempted`: Virtual router has changed to Active state because it has preempted other Active virtual router. * `active_no_response`: Virtual router has changed to Active state because it didn't recieve any advertisement packet from other virtual router and active down timer was expired.

active_router.description: Specifies the IP address of the active router.

active_to_init_last_change.description: Epoch time of the last change from active to init state.

active_to_standby_last_change.description: Epoch time of the last change from active to standby state.

init_to_active_last_change.description: Epoch time of the last change from init to active state.

init_to_standby_last_change.description: Epoch time of the last change from init to standby state.

is_active_local.description: Specifies if this router is active.

mode.description: Specifies mode of the VRRP group. * `standby`: A router configured in a VR as a Standby to the Owner configured for the same VR. There must be a minimum of one Standby in a VR to support VRRP operation if the Owner fails. Every Standby is created with a configurable priority that determines the precedence for becoming the Active of the VR if the Owner or another Standby operating as the Active becomes unavailable.Default standby priority value is `100`. * `owner`: The router configured in a VR to own the virtual IP address associated with the VR.(The virtual IP address for the VR must be configured as a real IP address on the interface on which the VR is configured. The Owner is automatically configured with the highest VRRP router priority value `255` in the VR and operates as the Active router for the VR unless it becomes unavailable to the network. * `uninitialized`: The operational mode for the VR entry has not been yet specified. The mode is set to owner or active after an IP address associated for the VR.

standby_to_active_last_change.description: Epoch time of the last change from standby to active state.

standby_to_init_last_change.description: Epoch time of the last change from standby to init state.

state.description: Specifies current state of the VRRP group.

state_duration.description: The amount of time in seconds since VRRP group moved to this state.

stats_discontinuity_time.description: Epoch time at which discontinuity of vrrpv3 statistics for this virtual router were experienced.

vrrp_ipv4_virtual_address_entries.description: Number of IPv4 VRRP virtual addresses configured on this virtual router.

vrrp_ipv6_virtual_address_entries.description: Number of IPv6 VRRP virtual addresses configured on this virtual router.

advertise_interval.description: Specifies VRRP hello interval time in milliseconds.

preempt_delay_time.description: Specifies a time in seconds that this router will wait before taking control of the virtual IP address that will allow it to route packets.  In normal VRRP operation, one router(say Router-1) is in the Active state and one router (Router-2) is in the Standby state. Router-1 provides the default gateway for the hosts. If Router-1 goes down for any reason, the Standby router, Router-2, provides the default gateway for the host. When Router-1 comes back on line (fail-back), it takes control of the VIP, and begins sending out VRRP advertisement packets at regular intervals. The standby router receives the VRRP advertisements and transitions to the standby state.  When OSPF is also enabled on the routers and a fail-back event occurs, the active router immediately takes control of the VIP and provides the default gateway functionality. If the OSPF has not converged, the route table in the active router may not be completely populated. When hosts send packets to the default gateway, the active router may not know where to send them and packets may be dropped.  The Preempt Delay Timer allows user to configure a period of time before the VR takes control of the VIP. It doesn't transition to active state until the timer period expires.

version.description: VRRP protocol version. VRRPv3 supports usage of IPv4 and IPv6 addresses while VRRPv2 only supports IPv4 addresses.

virtual_mac.description:
Reference Resource: [MAC](#/MAC)
Specifies the virtual MAC address for the VR that gets added to the MAC table when the VR becomes active.

parameters.name: Interface.name
parameters.description:
Reference Resource: [Port](#/Port)
The port name. For non-bonded ports, the port name is the same as the associated interface name. The name must otherwise be unique across all ports and interfaces of the system.

parameters.description: Columns to display.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Depth to traverse.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: Select configuration, status and/or statistics. Default is all categories.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Filter rows by attribute values.  Format: attribute:value

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Count the number of rows found.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Entity-tag value for representation comparison (see RFC 7232 - Conditional Requests - section 3.2)

parameters.description: Entity-tag value for representation comparison (see RFC 7232 - Conditional Requests - section 3.2)

accept_mode_disable.description: Set this value to `true`, to disable the accept mode. If accept mode is enabled, routes for vritual IP addresses will be installed and VR will accept the packets destined to virtual IP addresses. If accept mode is disabled, routes for virtual IP addresses will not be installed hence VR will not accept any packet destined to virtual IP addresses.

admin_enable.description: Set this value to `true`, to activate the VR instance.

auth_key.description: Authentication key to be used with VRRPv2 advertisements. This does not take effect if the VRRP version is VRRPv3. If not set, VRRP authentication is not operational on that VR.

auth_mode.description: Specifies the authentication mode to be used when exchanging VRRP packets. This is only applicable when VRRP version is VRRPv2.  `text`: a clear-text password is included in VRRP advertisements.  `md5` : an Authentication Header(AH) is added to the IPv4 headers of the VRRP advertisement packets.  `none` : VRRP advertisement packets are not authenticated. This does not take effect if the VRRP version is VRRPv3.

bfd_peer_addresses.description: Specifies all potential BFD peers. Active will establish BFD sessions to all peers. Standby will establish BFD session to the active only.

group-id.description:
Reference Resource: [VRRP](#/VRRP)
The port's VRRP groups (or VR instances) for IPv6 address family. A maximum of `32` VRRP groups can be assigned to a port.

ip_address.description: Specifies a virtual IPv4 or IPv6 address for the VR instance. For an owner, the virtual IP must be one of the IP addresses configured on the interface for that VR. For a standby, the virtual IP must match the virtual IP of the owner. The owner and the standbys using a given virtual IP must all belong to the same network or subnet. For IPv6, VR's first address should be link local address. After the primary link local IPv6 address is configured on the VR, user can add the global IPv6 addresses.  This column, also specifies the interface's IP address to designate as the source for VRRP advertisements from the VR. By default primary IP address of real interface is used as source for VRRP advertisements. Source IP configuration parameter is for IPv4 only. IPv6 doesn't have a source IP address configuration parameter. For IPv6, the source IP address is the link-local address of the real interface over which the packet is transmitted.

ip_address_secondary.description: Specifies secondary IPv4 or IPv6 addresses for the VRRP group. You must configure a primary address before you are able to configure secondary addresses.

preempt_disable.description: Set this value to `true`, to disable preempt mode. When mode is enabled, a Standby router coming up with a higher priority than another Standby that is currently operating as Active will take over the Active function. When the mode is disabled, the protocol prevents higher-priority Standby from taking over the Active operation from a lower-priority Standby. This mode does not prevent an Owner router from resuming the Active function after recovering from being unavailable. Also, the VR instance must be disabled (that is, set "admin_enable" to `false`) when setting this field.

priority.description: The priority value of the VR.

advertise_interval.description: Specifies VRRP hello interval time in milliseconds.

preempt_delay_time.description: Specifies a time in seconds that this router will wait before taking control of the virtual IP address that will allow it to route packets.  In normal VRRP operation, one router(say Router-1) is in the Active state and one router (Router-2) is in the Standby state. Router-1 provides the default gateway for the hosts. If Router-1 goes down for any reason, the Standby router, Router-2, provides the default gateway for the host. When Router-1 comes back on line (fail-back), it takes control of the VIP, and begins sending out VRRP advertisement packets at regular intervals. The standby router receives the VRRP advertisements and transitions to the standby state.  When OSPF is also enabled on the routers and a fail-back event occurs, the active router immediately takes control of the VIP and provides the default gateway functionality. If the OSPF has not converged, the route table in the active router may not be completely populated. When hosts send packets to the default gateway, the active router may not know where to send them and packets may be dropped.  The Preempt Delay Timer allows user to configure a period of time before the VR takes control of the VIP. It doesn't transition to active state until the timer period expires.

version.description: VRRP protocol version. VRRPv3 supports usage of IPv4 and IPv6 addresses while VRRPv2 only supports IPv4 addresses.

parameters.name: Interface.name
parameters.description:
Reference Resource: [Port](#/Port)
The port name. For non-bonded ports, the port name is the same as the associated interface name. The name must otherwise be unique across all ports and interfaces of the system.
